findings.title: Windows taskkill failure on an already-exited child masks the timeout and leaves descendants
findings.message: On Windows, any non-zero taskkill exit is treated as failed cleanup. taskkill also exits non-zero when the direct child has already exited, for example when only a descendant still holds the capture pipes. In that case the timeout path raises ChildCleanupError and the original TimeoutExpired is lost. A direct child that has exited is also not terminated by taskkill /PID, so its leftover descendants are not killed either.
findings.suggestion: Skip taskkill when process.poll() is not None, or accept the 'process not found' exit code (128) as success. Use a Job Object if descendants must be killed after the direct child has exited.
findings.evidence: raise ChildCleanupError("Windows taskkill could not confirm owned process-tree termination")

findings.title: Descendants are not cleaned up on the normal exit path
findings.message: The owned process group is killed only when communicate raises. When the direct child exits normally (success or non-zero status), its descendants are never terminated. Without capture pipes, a background grandchild outlives the call. With pipes, communicate returns only when the grandchild closes them. This contradicts the module's stated 'owned process-group cleanup' guarantee, and the finally block kills only the direct child.
findings.suggestion: After the direct child exits, call terminate_owned_group(process) best-effort on every path, tolerating ProcessLookupError, so no descendants remain after run_child returns.

findings.title: Timing-sensitive test may be flaky because pidfile is written within 0.5s
findings.message: The test relies on a 0.5s deadline during which two Python interpreters must start and the PID file must be written. On a slow or loaded CI host the timeout can fire before the pidfile exists, so `assertTrue(pidfile.is_file())` fails spuriously. The test also asserts total time < 3s, which adds further timing sensitivity. This is the only real-descendant acceptance test, and it is part of check.sh.
findings.suggestion: Make the parent signal readiness (write the pidfile) and give a generous timeout only for the sleeping phase. For example, use a longer timeout such as 5s and have the parent exit the wait early, or have the test poll for the pidfile before the deadline expires.
findings.evidence: child.run_child([sys.executable, "-c", parent, str(pidfile), grandchild], timeout=0.5, capture_output=True, text=True)

finding.title: Public SDK inventory hardcodes distribution_audit "pending", contradicting the approved gate
finding.message: license_inventory always writes distribution_audit as "pending", even for a public build. release_gates only lets a public build through when third_party_distribution_audit is "approved". The shipped THIRD_PARTY_INVENTORY.json therefore contradicts the release metadata and the gate, and consumers or automation reading it get a wrong audit status. The status is also non-deterministic with respect to the release metadata.
finding.suggestion: Pass the release metadata (or the public flag) into license_inventory and set distribution_audit from metadata["third_party_distribution_audit"]. Keep "pending" only for private builds.
